note: Answer key for the memory-index dry-run (memory-index-dry-run-plan.md). Seeding briefs are work-diary prose over a simulated 5-week strutil arc; facts are embedded, never labeled. Quiz sessions and judges receive questions only; the judge receives expected answers per question. Traps (category false_memory) have expected=ABSTAIN.

seeding_briefs.brief: Kickoff session for the strutil push toward 1.0. Getting organised: Dana is taking the lead maintainer role, with Priya and Marcus as the other two maintainers. We settled the release rhythm - monthly releases, cut on the first Monday of each month. CI gets a hard wall-clock budget of 40 minutes per run; anything slower has to be split or dropped. The whole 1.0 effort is going under the codename 'Granite' so it's easy to track in discussions. Nothing to code yet today - just make sure the project is in a sane state: run the checks in run_checks.py and confirm they pass, and fix nothing unless something is actually broken.

Priya filed a bug this morning: slugify mangles accented input - her example was slugify("Crème Brûlée") coming out as 'cr-me-br-l-e' instead of anything readable. After looking at options we agreed the right fix is a Unicode NFKD fold before the existing regex, and we're scheduling that fix for the 0.9.1 release rather than rushing it. Today: reproduce her example by adding a check to run_checks.py that documents the CURRENT (wrong) behaviour with a TODO comment naming the planned NFKD fix - do not implement the fix itself yet.

Two things from this week's sync. First, config: people keep asking for comments in settings.json; we decided settings stay plain strict JSON for now - comment support was rejected as not worth a custom parser. Second, Marcus ran the first benchmark pass: slugify sits at 1.2 microseconds per operation on the reference box, which we're recording as the baseline nothing may regress past. Today: add a one-line note to the README's development section stating the perf baseline (1.2 µs/op for slugify) so contributors see it.

Started assembling the 0.9.0 release checklist. So far it has two items: fold the changelog, and sign the git tag. Also settled after some back and forth: minimum supported Python moves to 3.11 - the tomllib and typing features we want make anything older painful. Today: create a RELEASE.md at the repo root containing the checklist as it currently stands (just those two items, as a markdown checklist), and note the new Python floor in it.

CI got slow, so the budget decision from kickoff is revised: the wall-clock budget is now 25 minutes, down from the original 40. Separately it's now official that Marcus owns the benchmark suite going forward - route perf questions to him. Today: nothing code-side except hygiene - make sure run_checks.py still passes, and tighten any obviously slow check if one exists (do not add dependencies).

Release checklist grew during review practice: add 'wheel audit' and 'README badge check' to the 0.9.0 checklist, after changelog fold and tag signing. Also we argued about truncate() again and CONFIRMED the existing semantics: the ellipsis counts toward the limit, and a limit shorter than the ellipsis returns a bare slice - that behaviour is now locked as the documented contract. Today: update RELEASE.md with the two new checklist items, and expand truncate()'s docstring one line to state the locked contract explicitly.

Cadence change: monthly releases were too slow for the bugfix flow, so releases now go out biweekly, cut on Thursdays. The first-Monday-monthly rhythm from kickoff is dead. Also the docs question got settled: the documentation site will be hosted on ReadTheDocs. Today: record the new cadence in RELEASE.md (replace any mention of the old rhythm), and add a 'Docs' line to README pointing at ReadTheDocs as the future docs home.

Two release moves. The NFKD unicode fix originally scheduled for 0.9.1 got pulled forward - it ships in 0.9.0 after all, Priya pushed for it and nobody objected. And the checklist is now final at five items: changelog fold, tag signing, wheel audit, README badge check, and a Priya sign-off as the last gate. Today: implement the NFKD fold in slugify (normalize, strip combining marks, then the existing regex), update the run_checks.py expectation for Crème Brûlée to 'creme-brulee', and bring RELEASE.md to the final five-item list.

The JSON-comments decision from week 2 is reversed: settings will support comments after all, via a JSONC comment-strip preprocessor in load_settings - plain-JSON files must keep working unchanged. Also welcoming Sofia, who joins specifically to own Windows CI. Today: implement the comment-strip fallback in config.py (try plain JSON first, strip // and /* */ comments and retry on failure), and add a check covering a commented settings snippet.

Wrap-up session before the quiet week. We defined the 1.0 gate: 1.0 ships only when there are zero open correctness bugs AND every Granite checklist item is complete - features explicitly do not block it. Today: give RELEASE.md a short '1.0 gate' section stating exactly that rule, and run the full checks one last time to confirm green.
